      page for Stanisław Chełmski's claim against the Fiscus (the Prussian treasury)
      over the 12,000 ducats he lent Prusimski. Two points would first need your ruling:
      the suit's date (the copy reads 19 March 1799 but its own chronology fits 1796)
      and the figure (12,000 ducats in the documents against 36,000 in Triebenfeld's
      memorandum of 1815). Say whether to build them and which date and figure to use.
      Options: Build both with the documents' date and figure / Build after you check the date / Do not build
      Concerns: [Nr. 421](/sources/ihagrrep7cnr421/), [Stanisław Chełmski](/people/stanislaw-chelmski/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "I. HA GR, Rep. 7 C, Nr. 421: Chełmski's claim on Prusimski, 1799 (added and published 2026-11-21)".

- [ ] **Person entry for Massow, and four words needing scans** (`t114-person-entry-for-massow`, question). Under the official's note of 18 October 1799 the file is signed "Massow"; the state
      handbook of 1799-1801 makes von Massow the minister of justice for South Prussia,
      so Claude thinks the signer is very probably Julius Eberhard von Massow. Should he
      get a person entry, and should the text say "Massow" plainly or with a note? Also
      open are words from the sweep of Oe 1 Bü 9454 that need the scans, chiefly letter
      21's "an die Genuenſter Fürſt", where both readers read "Fürſt" but not the word
      before it.
      Options: Person entry, name with a note / Person entry, plain "Massow" / No person entry
      Concerns: [Nr. 421](/sources/ihagrrep7cnr421/), [Oe 1 Bü 9454](/sources/oe1bu9454/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "I. HA GR, Rep. 7 C, Nr. 421: Chełmski's claim on Prusimski, 1799 (added and published 2026-11-21)".

## The place-name databases and gazetteer candidate places

- [ ] **Three open gazetteer questions: Czarna Góra, Orliny, Augustynów** (`t117-three-open-gazetteer-questions`, question). Czarna Góra is the hill by Wrąbczynek ("folw. pod Czarną górą", Słownik t. XIV, p. 16);
      you answered "unsure" and it was not added. Orliny (Słownik t. VII, p. 587: a
      colony on the Biała stream, gmina Rzgów, 54 houses, 546 inhabitants) may be the
      gazetteer's Orlina Duża; say whether they are one place. Augustynów's inhabitants
      are 358 in the gazetteer and 368 in the converted Słownik text (t. XV, p. 51); the
      page image would settle it.
      Options: Orliny is Orlina Duża / Orliny is a different place / Augustynów: 358 / Augustynów: 368
      Concerns: [Wrąbczynek](/places/wrabczynek/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The gazetteer's candidate places (2026-11-21)".

- [ ] **Find the Kodeks entry of 1341 cited in the Pyzdry footnote** (`t118-find-the-kodeks-entry`, task). A footnote on Pyzdry cites an entry of 1341 in the Kodeks Dyplomatyczny Wielkopolski,
      vol. 2, but gives no entry number, so it is not in the edition's holding of the
      Kodeks. docs/MISSING_SOURCES.md still lists it. If you can find the number in the
      volumes on your drive, send it and it can be added.
      Concerns: [Kodeks Dyplomatyczny Wielkopolski](/sources/kdw/), [Pyzdry](/places/pyzdry/)

## Places, people and the glossary (site overhaul, planned 2026-11-24)

- [ ] **Supply the literature's title pages for thumbnails** (`t119-supply-the-literature-s`, waiting). On the redesigned Literature page each work is meant to show a thumbnail of its title
      page. You said you would supply the title pages that exist; until then no typeset
      tiles are shown instead. Nothing to do until you send them.

- [ ] **Rule on the open points found in the rewritten summaries** (`t122-open-points-from-the`, task). When all 649 English summaries were rewritten, these points came up. Letter 64 is dated
      6 December 1809 but reports Queen Louise's death, which was on 19 July 1810.
      Letter 232 is dated 16 June 1811 but its content belongs to 1812, and letter 257
      (7 October 1814) cites a representation of 23 October. Recipients or writers do
      not fit the text in letters 001a, 036, 047, 224 and 072. In letter 74c, the "Court
      of Appeal" is the Superior Court of Justice at Berlin. Nr. 421 gives the cabinet
      order as 14 September 1796 in document 1 but "the 16th" in documents 4 and 5. Oe 1
      Bü 14525, document 14: the base is 199,463 Reichsthaler, not 186,943. Please rule
      on each.
      Concerns: [Oe 1 Bü 9454](/sources/oe1bu9454/), [Nr. 421](/sources/ihagrrep7cnr421/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The summaries rewritten (2026-11-25, docs/PLACES_PEOPLE_GLOSSARY_PLAN.md, E2)".

- [ ] **Write glossary entries for desiatin, sazhen and mansi** (`t123-write-glossary-entries-for`, claude). The Russian land measures desiatin and sazhen, and the Latin land measure mansus (plural
      mansi), appear in documents and summaries but have no glossary entry yet. Claude
      will write them, checked against a reference work, with no answer needed from you.
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The summaries rewritten (2026-11-25, docs/PLACES_PEOPLE_GLOSSARY_PLAN.md, E2)".

- [ ] **German summaries to be written all at once, later** (`t124-german-summaries-to-be`, waiting). The English summaries were rewritten to the new house style on 2026-11-25, but the
      German ones were not. At your word they will be redone together in one German
      pass. Nothing to do until you give that word.

- [ ] **Triebenfeld's death: is the office note's 13 April 1816?** (`t125-triebenfeld-s-death-is`, question). Peter August von Triebenfeld's last letter is of 31 January 1816. The only statement
      that he was dead is an office note on Zerboni's report, headed "Paris 18 Nov 1815"
      but ending "on 13 April" with no year (Nr. 12765, document 10). His page says he
      died between 31 January and 13 April 1816, taking that 13 April for 1816. Is that
      right?
      Options: Yes, 1816 / No, a different year
      Concerns: [Triebenfeld](/people/triebenfeld/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The relevant people's pages (2026-11-25, docs/PLACES_PEOPLE_GLOSSARY_PLAN.md, C6-C7)".

- [ ] **The Prince's age: keep birth year 1746?** (`t126-the-prince-s-age`, question). In November 1814 Triebenfeld wrote that Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen was "nearly 66",
      but the reference works' birth date of 31 January 1746 makes him 68. The edition
      keeps 1746; confirm or change it.
      Options: Keep 1746 / Change the birth year
      Concerns: [Prince Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen](/people/hohenlohe/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The relevant people's pages (2026-11-25, docs/PLACES_PEOPLE_GLOSSARY_PLAN.md, C6-C7)".

- [ ] **Paweł Prusimski's office: which title?** (`t127-pawe-prusimski-s-office`, question). The press report of 1754 calls Paweł Prusimski chamberlain, the decree of 1784 sub-
      chamberlain (subcamerarius), and one passage of its English podskarbi (treasurer).
      His page says the King's chamberlain. Which title should the edition use?
      Options: Chamberlain / Sub-chamberlain / Treasurer (podskarbi)
      Concerns: [Prusimski family](/people/prusimski/)
      Full discussion: NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, "The relevant people's pages (2026-11-25, docs/PLACES_PEOPLE_GLOSSARY_PLAN.md, C6-C7)".

- [ ] **Chełmski's loan to Prusimski: 12,000 or 36,000 ducats?** (`t128-chemski-s-loan-to`, question). Stanisław Chełmski's note of 1794 is for 12,000 ducats, but Triebenfeld's memorandum of
      1815 says Prusimski pledged Trąbczyn to Chełmski for 36,000 ducats. The pages
